# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

16	## Summary
17	
18	Derelict Authoring (Handmade Kits) is the MVP's content layer: the hand-built data for the three ships the first build contains (the home-ship the player wakes in, a cold wreck and a hot wreck), the kit manifest they are assembled from, every placement table that fills them, and the content lint that holds it all honest; it owns authored files, not runtime state (no state block, hook, mutator or read view). Everything authored is a physical fact in an owner's schema (a Graph subject with a `def_id` and `hp`, a Layout rectangle, an Item DB def, an Emitter placement), so a wreck reads as a body with a cause of death, a usable organ and a cost of extraction, never as a level or a loot room. Read it to author or lint a ship, to see the eight faults, the part ledger and the numbers that make the first ten minutes work, or to learn the record and lint shapes Procedural Derelict Generation will assemble from later.
19	
20	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Feature` — Priority: `MVP` — Key deps: `Ship Section & Layout Data Model` (designed), `Item & Module Database` (designed), `Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query` (designed); hard: Life-Support Graph (reclassified by the design review *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*); soft: Failure & Trail, Interaction, Suit & Equipment, 2D Lighting (designed), Ship Body & Interior Physics (designed); downstream: Web Map & Transit, Boarding & Salvage (undesigned)
21	
22	## Overview
23	
24	Derelict Authoring (Handmade Kits) is the **content layer of the MVP**: the hand-built, data-only description of the three ships the player will ever see in the first build — the **home-ship** they wake in (the first derelict they learn to read), a cold wreck (**derelict A**) and a hot wreck (**derelict B**) — together with the **kit manifest** those ships are assembled from, every **placement table** that fills them (Graph nodes with `def_id` and `hp`, the eight live faults and their dried companions, lamps, the one beacon, loose parts and glowsticks, sockets, hardpoints, plate positions, spawn cells, the one visible unknown per wreck, and the reserved-but-empty story-slot list), and the **content lint** that holds all of it honest. It owns authored files, not runtime state: it registers no state block, no hook, no mutator and no read view (DA-1). Layout builds its files, the Graph instantiates its nodes, the Emitter instantiates its lights, Interaction places its loose items, and each of them owns its own schema, physics, vocabulary or light data. This GDD owns *what is authored* and the rules every authored file (and, later, every procedurally assembled one) must satisfy.
25	
26	**How the player meets it.** They never meet "authoring"; they meet places, and the honesty of those places. The player wakes in the home-ship's cryo bay (one Tungsten lamp guttering, a coolant drip frosting a line across the floor to the far wall), closes a breaker, feels the room warm, follows the frost to the fitting that failed and patches it. They then ride a pod to a cold, black wreck whose only light is somebody else's lantern; they read dried trails by the chest lamp's beam alone, decide whether to feed a dead branch (and wake a machine that will start failing again, twice as fast as at home) or leave it dark, and carry a scrubber home. On a second sortie they cross a hot wreck with a scrammed reactor and a vented bay, and weld that wreck's dock onto their own ship. Every object they read, light, cut, carry or feed in the MVP is a record in this system's files; a playtester should be able to point at the weld seam afterwards and say which side was the original ship (Layout experience target X-1, answered here by the `_worn` kit, DA-5).
27	
28	**What the game loses without it.** The Graph would have nothing to instantiate, the Item DB nothing to place, the weld nothing to join, and the eight MVP faults no home; the concept's MVP item 1 (authored places) would be unmet; and the Vertical Slice's Procedural Derelict Generation would have no kit vocabulary, record shapes or rule set to assemble (the kit definition is what procgen later assembles, so the manifest, the placement shapes and every lint are written as reusable data rules, not as one-off floor plans, DA-39 to DA-44).
29	
30	**Index wording reconciled.** The index row calls for a "hand-built Foundry-dialect derelict and spawn ship" and says "MVP uses two handmade derelicts"; the concept's MVP item 1 reads "one handmade spawn derelict and one handmade target derelict, with an abstracted pod hop". Six designed GDDs (Life-Support Graph LS-26, Ship Section & Layout LY-25, Emitter State EM-24, Failure & Trail FT-38, 2D Lighting AC-LO-60, Save/Load SL-18) already size **three** sections, 14 compartments and eight faults. This GDD therefore authors **three ship templates**: `home_ship` (the spawn derelict, where the cryo bay is), `derelict_a` and `derelict_b` (the "two handmade derelicts" the player sorties to), plus a stub `pod` template for the transit leg (provisional, DA-3). Two pod hops; no pre-welded start. The concept and index wording ("one target", "a pod hop") are summaries and a wording refresh is routed, not edited (Cross-References).
31	
32	| Scale at a glance (MVP, design counts) | `home_ship` | `derelict_a` | `derelict_b` | Total |
33	|---|---|---|---|---|
34	| Rooms (compartments) | 5 | 4 | 5 | 14 |
35	| Room volume `V` (tiles) | 182 | 118 | 149 | 449 (74.8 % of `TILES_WORLD_MVP` 600, the sum of all three; the largest legal loaded set is smaller, D.1) |
36	| Graph nodes | 42 | 27 | 35 | 104 (within the Graph's MVP bound of 120) |
37	| Hardpoints (module nodes + the home spare heater slot + the two vacant scrubber slots, DA-47) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | 29 | 18 | 22 | 69 |
38	| LOAD nodes (lamps, the beacon lamp, door motors, heaters) | 11 | 7 | 8 | 26 |
39	| Fixtures (lamp housings) | 8 | 6 | 7 | 21 |
40	| Dock status glows (DA-46; self-powered, `node_ref` 0, not lamp housings; counted conservatively against the fixture caps in D.3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | 1 | 1 | 1 | 3 |
41	| Live faults of the eight | 4 | 2 | 2 | 8 |
42	| Sockets | 1 | 0 | 1 | 2 (one mating pair) |

46	
47	**What this GDD is not.** It is not the template schema (Layout), the structural lint (Layout), the Graph's physics, the Item DB's vocabulary, the Emitter's light data, a pixel (the art-director and technical-artist draw), a procedural generator (VS-A), a story (no text, no names, no bodies), a combat encounter set (no authored entity placement) or a loot economy (no rarity, no rolls). Where this GDD touches an owner's rule it cites the rule id and never restates its value with a different number.
48	
49	**Pillar alignment.** *Pillar 1 (primary), verbatim:* "Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth. Only instruments and perception can be wrong." The authored places are where that sentence is made true or false: every cause of death in a wreck is a dried trail on a real Graph subject, every light has a source the player can walk to, and nothing authored is decoration pretending to be evidence. *Design test applied to content:* "a hidden stat vs. a visibly leaking pipe → the pipe": author the pipe. *Pillar 5 (primary, content side), verbatim:* "The outer ring is kept unsafe by depletion and wear (scrubbers degrade, salvage runs out), so there is no safe place to farm forever." This system owns the placement numbers of that sentence: the finite part ledger (5 parts against 7 full repairs, 714 permille, DA-25), the authored `hp` of every salvageable module, and G-0 (the MVP is survivable with zero parts). *Design test:* "safe farming vs. scarcity that pushes inward → scarcity." Pillars 2, 3 and 4 are served indirectly and named in the header; the anti-pillars are guard rails (Player Fantasy, DA-37).
50	
51	
52	## Player Fantasy
53	
54	**Framing: the Forensic Salvager (direct).** *Read the dead ship, then decide what it costs to take its heart.* Derelict Authoring has no verb of its own and no screen; what the player touches is its output — three places and the honesty with which they were built — so the fantasy is a **reading fantasy with a price tag**, not a power fantasy. A dead ship is a sentence the chest lamp's beam can read: it tells you how it died, what it can spare and what it will cost you to take it, and it never lies, because it has no power left to lie with (art bible 2.6: dried trails "teach the loop grammar on a ship that cannot lie because it has no power to lie with"). Every place in the MVP was built so that one sweep of the beam answers three questions — who built this, what happened to it, has the web come in (art bible 6.0) — and then asks the only question the game cares about: *what will it cost to take it?* The concept's base is "a body they assembled from the corpses of other ships" (Core Fantasy): this system authors the corpses, and each must be read as a body with a cause of death, a usable organ and a cost of extraction, never as a level, a dungeon or a loot room.
55	
56	(orchestrator ruling: three framings were weighed. A, "The Forensic Salvager" (direct, serves P1 and P5 co-primary), is adopted. B, "Somebody Else's Lantern" (the lure of the one lit thing on a dead ship) describes one beat per wreck and over-promises — a lure that promises a person and delivers a battery is a broken contract — so it is adopted only as the **first beat** of the anchor moment below. C, "The Organ Donor" (harvest) belongs to Modular Ship Assembly and would push flesh language into authored places, blurring the sane palette that P1 reserves for sanity leaks; "corpse" stays a concept-level metaphor and this GDD's own vocabulary stays mechanical.)
57	
58	**Primary anchor moment: "You woke it. Now it is a clock." (derelict A, first sortie).**
59	1. *Transit.* From the pod, derelict A is black except one Tungsten point: the residual lamp `lamp_a_life` (DA-27) on a battery that runs down only while you are aboard. It is somebody else's lantern.
60	2. *Arrival.* Beam only (art bible 2.6). Dust in the cone. Under the closed door of the machine room a dried frost fan creeps across the sill — a dead coolant fault authored per DA-17. The eye follows trail to source to hatch (art bible 6.5).
61	3. *The lock is the physics.* Inside the cold room the branch is dead because a CABLE_JUNCTION sits at `hp` 2000 with a radial scorch at its box. There is no keycard. The spare `mod_breaker_junction` lies on a shelf in the life-support room, beside the residual lamp and the failed scrubber (the light points at the reason to board).
62	4. *The decision.* Swap the breaker and the dead branch wakes (DA-13 (c)): lanterns come on, which the web can see (P3), and the bus battery that feeds them is now a clock you can watch run down: about 101 s on the full bus before the pump lantern goes dark (D.16) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was "a pump that was starved is now a live clock that runs at twice home speed"; no A subject has an endogenous wear clock once fed, so the beat promises only what A delivers)*. Or leave it dark, cut the failed scrubber by beam alone (the first V8), and carry it home quiet. The decision is taken at the door of the coldest room aboard, and feeding the wreck has exactly one computed benefit: the heater lifts that lethal room out of damaging cold for about 12.9 minutes (D.22), the only time it can be worked in unhurried, and it lasts a bus battery's lifetime, not a base's (DA-28). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
63	5. *The cost lands.* Waking the wreck was the player's act, so the lit lanterns the web can see, the bus running out and the cold coming back to the machine room about 12.0 minutes after the pump goes dark (D.22) are their consequence, never the game's ambush *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
64	
65	The sentence we want overheard: *"If I power this, it starts dying again, and it'll be loud."* The rule behind it is stated once, in the player's terms, and is the only statement of derelict time behaviour that may appear in player-facing or design prose (it is the Graph's three mechanisms, DA-13): **a derelict does not degrade while you are away; a dead branch stays quiet until you feed it; while you are aboard, whatever can wear, wears twice as fast.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier "once you are aboard and it is fed, it fails twice as fast as home" was wrong in scope, because DA-13 (b) compresses wear on every loaded derelict section whether or not it is powered: fault #7 runs dark on B from the first loaded step, and welded B keeps compression. User ruling D45 stands.)* The two secondary anchors are *warmth is spent, not owned* (the home-ship wake: the EMERGENCY lamp, the breaker, the room flooding with light and the heater's slow warm-up, about 6.5 minutes to COMFORT, D.18) and *which side was ours?* (the weld seam against the maintained and `_worn` kit). The playtest-checkable targets (X-DA-1 to X-DA-11; X-DA-8 is the anchor moment's own "leave it dark" test, X-DA-9 guards the treadmill, X-DA-10 guards the first sortie to B and X-DA-11 the first scrubber install at home *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*) are written in Game Feel and Acceptance Criteria.
66	
67	**Framing scope and the forward line (VS-B).** Co-op is outside MVP, so the Forensic Salvager is a solo fantasy here: one boarder reading the ship alone, and "we keep it alive minute by minute" is carried by *warmth is spent, not owned*. For Vertical Slice B (co-op) the same authored places need no schema change: a wreck's legibility (the dried trail on a real fitting, the dark lantern, the frost line) is exactly what a boarder reads aloud to the ship-keeper, so Fellowship (MDA rank 3) and the human channel (P4) build on these places as they stand.
68	
69	**Pillar anchors, verbatim.** P1: "Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth." P5: "Risk and reward map to depth in the web. The outer ring is kept unsafe by depletion and wear ... so there is no safe place to farm forever." P2: "Every breach is preceded by a tell a careful player could have perceived." P3: "The players' light, noise, power use and restraint raise or lower its attention ... shown in the world ... never as a hidden meter." P4: "No lie is unfalsifiable: the truth is always available through the physical world, a second instrument, a saner crewmate, the human channel, or time."
70	
71	| Pillar | Rank here | What the player feels because of authoring |
72	|---|---|---|
73	| P1 The World Never Lies | PRIMARY | "I can read this." Every cause of death is a dried trail on a real fitting; every light has a source I can walk to; nothing in a wreck is decoration pretending to be a fault. |
74	| P5 Deeper Is Richer, Loss Is Not Total | PRIMARY | "This wreck can spare a few parts, not everything I need." The ledger is finite and visible as objects on the floor; choosing what to carry is the moment of value. |
75	| P2 Dread Before Chaos | SERVES | "I saw it coming and I had somewhere to run." The tell is visible across the room and a closable door is within reach (DA-29). |
76	| P3 The Web Watches | SERVES | "If I power this, it will be seen." Waking a branch lights lanterns the web sees; leaving it dark is a real strategy (every room can be lit and un-lit, DA-22). |
77	| P4 Sanity Rewrites Reality | SERVES (indirect) | "The gauge says fixed; the frost says otherwise." Authoring supplies the physical witnesses that make every MVP false-state lie falsifiable (DA-34). |
78	
79	**Design test (this GDD's own).** Between an authored element the player is *told* about and one the player can *read* in one beam sweep and *verify* with one verb or one step, author the readable one; and if an authored element cannot be traced to a Graph subject, a Layout record or a `def_id`, it is not authored. Secondary test (P5): an extra part on the floor vs. a harder choice about which part to carry → the choice (the ledger sits at 714 permille inside the Item DB's advisory band, DA-25). The 714 permille is a placement statistic and not the source of the scarcity: the five parts map one-to-one onto the five part-repairable faults, so the felt scarcity is order and time (which repair waits for which sortie, which clocks run while the player is aboard), not a count that forces a choice between two needed parts. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
80	
81	**Under hallucination the fantasy deepens, it does not break.** Authored data is truth only: the Perception Filter (undesigned) corrupts presentation at runtime, never the template, and Layout already rules out any phantom-geometry record (LY-34). A wreck is where truth is cheapest to check, because the instruments are dark and the player is already reading the world. The content rule that makes P4's "no lie is unfalsifiable" true is the **truth-witness rule** (DA-34): every authored subject that the Filter could misrepresent — a gauge, a breaker, a valve, a salvageable module, a live fault — has at least one consequence-channel witness in the same compartment (a trail live or dried, a frost line, a lantern on or off, a lit or dark fixture on its branch, the room's own temperature or pressure effect). MVP ships hallucination class (b), false system states; the other three classes are named so authoring does not foreclose them.
82	
83	| P4 class | What authoring supplies so the lie is falsifiable | Worked example |
84	|---|---|---|
85	| (b) False system states (MVP) | the physical witness above; dead branches have dark fixtures, so "fixed" on a dark branch is checkable by looking at the lamp | A's pump reads "running" to a low-sanity player; the branch fixtures are dark and its lantern is off: the lie is visible in one sweep |
86	| (d) Phantom salvage (VS) | dried trails only where a dead fault was authored (FT:71's "cheap field read"); a finite ledger of real objects, none with violet or flesh pixels | a "pristine" scrubber with no trail in a room whose verdict says coolant failed: the absence of the authored trail is the field check before the carry home |
87	| (a) Phantom entities (VS) | nothing authored moves except periodic-motion media; dust, frost and door leaves a real entity's P1/P2 footprint can disturb | dust drifting in a sealed room is either the Tell or a lie; the frost line does not change for a lie |
88	| (c) Crewmates as horrors (VS) | a clear path of at least one tile, a 2 to 3 tile corridor, escape routes inside the fairness budget (DA-29) and a return path from every room: a sane player can always back away (a carrier at `V_CARRY` only after dropping cargo, Horror Entities C-HE-8); no authored one-way room where lethal friendly harm becomes unavoidable | a 3-tile corridor lets two crewmates pass without contact |
89	
90	The residual light is a real emitter with a battery clock (DA-27), so it obeys P1; the exterior transit view must read the Emitter's state and the Filter may neither fabricate nor erase it there (routed ask to Perception Filter and Web Map & Transit, both undesigned).
91	
92	**Reference techniques, adopted and rejected precisely.**
93	
94	| Source | Technique | Verdict | Exactly what we take or refuse |
95	|---|---|---|---|
96	| Project Zomboid | "every door is a decision" | ADOPT | few doors per route, each a closable escape (DA-29); doors are the only authored pacing device; no scripted door events |
97	| Pandorum (first ten minutes) | waking into wrongness, a chest lamp as the only warmth | ADOPT | the cryo wake; the chest point is the beam origin for every authored reach and clearance (user decision); not its last act (no creature set pieces) |
98	| Return of the Obra Dinn | reconstructing a death from frozen physical evidence | ADOPT the method, REJECT the delivery | adopt: cause read from physical state (dried trail, door leaf state, pod state); reject: text, names, a deduction UI, a "solved" state |
99	| Subnautica (the Aurora) | a visible wreck that pulls you before you board | ADOPT the pull, REJECT the radio | adopt: one visible unknown per wreck from transit; reject: radio messages, objective markers, signal pings |
100	| Alien: Isolation | handmade, line-of-sight-led spaces where the environment is the tutorial | ADOPT | the cryo bay teaches through one carried element; the beacon has line of sight to the cryo-bay door (DA-24) |
101	| Dead Space | blood-writing, corpses, audio logs | REJECT | no bodies, no text, no logs in MVP; empty suits only, and those are Vertical Slice |
102	| Barotrauma | interlocking systems failing on a boarded ship | ADOPT the breach rhythm, REJECT freeform sub editing | rooms are pre-shaped kit assemblies; sockets are pre-declared |
103	| Diablo and looter-shooters | rarity tiers, loot rolls | REJECT | richness by placement density, part supply and authored `hp` only |
104	| Lock-and-key level design | key items gate progress | REJECT, REPLACE | the lock is the physics: a dead branch gated by a broken junction and a spare breaker that is a real module with ports |
105	| Ambush scripting | monster closets on trigger volumes | REJECT | no authored instakill without a tell; Attention and Horror own escalation; authoring places no entity |
106	
107	**Anti-pillar guard rails (binding on every authored file; enforced in DA-37 and DA-40).** (1) *Not a freeform builder:* sections attach only at pre-declared sockets; modules are pre-shaped `def_id`s; the kit manifest is a content tool for authors and procgen, never a player palette. (2) *Not a combat game:* no authored enemy, spawn point, weapon cache, arena or turret; authoring leaves route data and light and power stimuli only. (3) *No intentional PvP:* no authored item whose only use is harming a crewmate, no armable trap, no reward placed where taking it requires another player to be exposed (review check). (4) *No authored linear story:* no chapters, cutscenes or scripted beats, ever; in MVP, story slots are `[]` and linted, and no text, names or bodies are placed. This is an MVP scope limit, not a permanent ban: the concept's anti-pillar is "not an authored linear story; lore is found and assembled", so Alpha lore fragments and the Narrative aesthetic stay open to the same kit schema, and what a later fragment may be is the narrative-director's to define. (5) *No win state:* no "wreck cleared", completion percentage or exhausted-wreck marker; a stripped wreck is a dark place with less in it. (6) *No meter:* no danger rating, salvage value, wreck tier, minimap or HUD icon for the visible unknown. (7) *Sane palette:* no flesh or violet in any kit piece or authored light. (8) *No fake evidence:* no loop-vocabulary decal that is not a Graph fault; no phantom, false or decoy record in any template. (9) *Dread before chaos:* every live fault has its endogenous tell; every exogenous hazard (B's breach) is entered by the player's own act; no authored one-way point (death is lethal including friendly fire, and MVP death is restart from the last autosave, which Save/Load owns). (10) *Restraint is possible:* every room can be dark; no forced-on authored light except the declared cryo EMERGENCY lamp and each wreck's residual lamp, both with physical sources.
108	
109	**Words the GDD uses for authored content:** dead, dried, cold, dark, spare, residual, wake (a branch), feed (power or coolant), cut, carry, weep (a seam), somebody else's lantern. **Words it does not:** loot, treasure, drop, rarity, tier, level, dungeon, cleared, enemy, spawn point (for entities), secret, hidden room, puzzle, key, lock (as mechanics), "dormant until powered" (it conflates three Graph mechanisms, DA-13).

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.

Suit's export is why the rule exists: with `INSUL_MC` 5000 an unpowered home-ship needs about 40 minutes to reach the shifted onset (SE-21), so a cold-hazard derelict room must be authored with an equilibrium temperature below the shifted cold onset or it is no hazard. It is the only lethal-cold room in MVP (B's hazard is heat and vacuum; B's heat room is `b_reactor`, next bullet). It is entered from `a_spine` (`T0` -12000 mC) through `door_a_spine_machine`, with a dried frost fan creeping out over the door sill, visible in the beam: the tell precedes the hazard (P2). Crossing is safe and lingering is lethal: at `T0` the room reaches CRITICAL cold in about 36 s and FAILED in about 109 s (Suit's D.4 with the Suit knobs; Formula D.10), so a seven-tile crossing takes 5.6 s carrying while the patch channel inside is the lethal act. The X-DA-8 reasons log (AC-DA-135) is the trigger for any later authored payoff, which the creative-director then owns (OQ-DA-43 options B to D)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. In-room work is budgeted by `t_work_max` (D.10): 25.2 s at `T0`, 13.8 s after 30 minutes unheated, 6.2 s at the equilibrium, module carried both ways. The junction `j_a_main` sits in `a_machine`: the swap is two channels (about 8 s) plus a 5.6 s crossing, 14 of the 25.2 s at `T0`, and the room needs 447 steps (44.7 s) after the breaker closes to pass the onset, so staying through them accrues about 4,200 of exposure against `TL_CRITICAL` 4,000 (gain 11 falling to 8); the order is swap, close the breaker, step back into `a_spine` for about 45 s and return (whether exposure recovers once the room is above the onset is Suit D.4's, cited and not assumed) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The "exactly one lethal room" invariant is a *build-state* invariant: opening the door between `a_spine` and `a_machine` mixes them by conduction, so the lint also prints the open-door projection.
464	- *Heat (derelict B, `b_reactor`, after V12; `[derived; Graph owner to confirm Q_src_room]`).* `b_reactor` is authored at `T0` 42000 mC (the HOT band, 40000 and up, LSG:96), 3000 mC under `HEAT_DMG_ONSET_MC` 45000 (registry). Suit's heat axis has no insulation shift (`e_heat` = `T` - `HEAT_DMG_ONSET_MC`, SE D.4), so the room is harmless as authored and its HOT shimmer is the standing tell. A SCRAMmed `r_b` has `Q_src` 0 and `T_mach` = `T_room` (LSG D.8), which is why V12 is not `BLOCKED` `STILL_HOT` (DA-35). **After V12** the restarted reactor leaks the uncaptured part of its heat into the room (`Q_src_room`; 516 dJ per step is the Graph's D.8 worked example, `[UNV: Graph]`) against a hull loss of `K_HULL` x 21 x (`T` - `T_AMB_MC`) / 100000 = 378 dJ per step at 42000 mC: the room reaches 45000 mC after about 2,770 steps (4.6 minutes, `tau_steps` 22,857) and settles near 68,300 mC (D.18). Authoring applies the carry bound to the **round trip** (R17: "and back"), the stricter reading, so a module can be carried out on the same reserve: `2 x tiles_one_way <= 56`. 640 - *Placement.* Exactly one glow per dock room, on the 96 x 96 docked-podcraft prop (kit gap K-3, DA-6): `fx_air_pod` in `airlock`, `fx_a_dock_pod` in `a_dock`, `fx_b_dock_pod` in `b_dock`; none in `pod_cabin`. Each is `node_ref` 0 (no Graph LOAD, no draw and no clock: its source is the docked pod's own standby cell, a diegetic fact of the prop, so it cannot drain, be cut, or be served or unserved by the room's bus), `switch_on` true at build, not switchable by PLAYER or SYSTEM origin and never modulated by Attention's tell, as the EMERGENCY lamp is (LO-20). The class id, and whether the Emitter refuses `set_switch` on it, are the Emitter's amendment `[PLACEHOLDER: Emitter EM-3 / EM-11]`. It is not a residual light: it has no island, no battery and no ledger.

641 - *Lit at the console.* The console anchor (the CONSOLE `subject_anchors` entry that OQ-DA-39 asks Layout for, within 2 tiles of `arrive_*`) must be lit by the glow alone. Arithmetic for the cap: `arrive_*` is 1 tile (48 px) clear of the prop, the prop's half-extent is 48 px, and the console is within 2 tiles (96 px) of `arrive_*`, so the worst glow-to-console distance is 48 + 48 + 96 = **192 px** (`DOCK_GLOW_CONSOLE_MAX_PX`). The Emitter's glow radius must therefore light a point 192 px away: `r_lit_glow` at least 192 px `[PLACEHOLDER: Emitter, derive at spike]`. `DOCK_GLOW_LIT_AT_CONSOLE` asserts the headless statement (lit at the console with the bus dead, every other emitter dark and the beam off), which is the state BS-19 cares about.

642 - *Separation from the visible unknown (art-director).* The glow must never read as the exterior unknown: its `output_pm` is at most `DOCK_GLOW_OUTPUT_MAX_PM` (provisional 250 permille of the residual lamp's `output_pm`, `[PLACEHOLDER: art-director, derive at the art spike]`), its hue class is not the residual lamp's Tungsten and is outside the flesh and violet bands (DA-37), and no dock room carries a `wall_port` piece, so the glow cannot appear in the exterior transit view. `VISIBLE_UNKNOWN_COMPETITOR` is unchanged because a dock room is never a host room (`a_life`, `b_breach`); `WAKE_SINGLE_LIGHT` is scoped to `cryo_bay` and is unaffected.

643 - *Counts.* Read conservatively as fixtures (D.3): the dock rooms stand at 2 of 4 (`airlock`), 2 of 3 (`a_dock`) and 2 of 3 (`b_dock`); the sets stand at S0 9, S1 16, S2 and S3 17 and S4 24 against 28. 1120:### D.18 Thermal drift (the cold-room invariant)

1079	### D.17 Reachable-set subject budget
1080	
1081	The `subject_budget_per_set` formula is defined as:
1082	
1083	`S_int(S) = F(S) + L_seed(S) + C` ; `S_total(S) = S_int(S) + PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE + ACTORS + HORRORS` ; `SUBJECT_BUDGET_SET iff S_int(S) > INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET or S_total(S) > MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` ; `I-7: INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET + PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE <= floor(3 x MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS / 4)` ; `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS_needed = ceil(4 x (INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET + PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE) / 3)`
1084	
1085	**Variables:**
1086	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
1087	|---|---|---|---|---|
1088	| `F` | int | 0 to 120 | IA D.10 and IA-37; declared interactables (hardpoints, two face subjects per door, valves, hull segments, sockets) | Home 50 (48 + 2 scrubber slots, DA-47), A 28, B 40 |
1089	| `L_seed` | int | 0 to 20 | DA-26 | Seeded loose placements still on the floor: home 2, A 4, B 4 (falls as the player collects) |
1090	| `C` | int | 0 to 18 | IA D.10 | Cap-stub worst case (at most 6 modules x 3 ports), counted once per set |
1091	| `PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE`, `ACTORS`, `HORRORS` (Interaction's `P`, `A`, `H`) | int | 24, 4, 2 | IA D.10, I-7; registry `subject_budget` | 30 together; `H` is `HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` 2 `[PLACEHOLDER: Horror]` Emitter HORROR subjects (one active plus one transient) |
1092	| `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` | int | 120 `[PLACEHOLDER: Interaction]` | registry (Interaction-owned, IA-37) | Content ceiling for the per-registration-window sum `W_int(p) = F + L_seed + C` at every authored body position, not for `S_int` over a loaded set (registry `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET`, `subject_budget`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* |
1093	| `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` | int | 192 `[PLACEHOLDER: Emitter]` (registry range 128 to 384) | registry (Emitter-owned) | Subject cap |
1094	
1095	**Output Range:** `S_int` 70 to 146 and `S_total` 100 to 176 in MVP content as loaded-set sums (the design review's 68 to 144 and 98 to 174 plus the two scrubber slots of DA-47) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
1096	**Example:**
1097	
1098	| Set | `F` | `L_seed` | `C` | `S_int` | vs 120 | `S_total` | vs 192 |
1099	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
1100	| S0 `{home}` | 50 | 2 | 18 | 70 | pass | 100 | pass |
1101	| S1 `{home, A}` | 78 | 6 | 18 | 102 | pass | 132 | pass |
1102	| S2, S3 `{home, B}` / `{home+B}` | 90 | 6 | 18 | 114 | pass (6 slack) | 144 | pass |
1103	| **S4 `{home+B, A}`** | 118 | 10 | 18 | **146** | **over by 26 as a loaded-set sum (not a registered state, see the D37 paragraph below)** | 176 | pass (16 slack) |
1104	
1105	I-7 check: 120 + 24 = 144 = floor(3 x 192 / 4) with `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` 192 `[PLACEHOLDER: Emitter]`, exactly at the limit. Raising the budget to 144 alone breaks I-7 (144 + 24 = 168 > 144) and needs `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` of ceil(4 x 168 / 3) = **224** (a two-owner change, Checkpoint rulings Q4 option 2). The Authoring-only diet (option 3) must remove at least 24 subjects from S4 to bring `S_int` to 120 (the Edge Cases list the named candidates and their readability cost).
1106	
1107	**Cumulative table with the instruments and pod consoles that OQ-DA-38 and OQ-DA-39 ask for (design review 2026-10-27).** Instruments are In-World Instruments' indicative placements (home 9, A 4 plus the second battery reading on A that partners `inst_b_a1_stock`, B 5) and the consoles are one per dock room (`airlock`, `a_dock`, `b_dock`); each is an Interaction subject. Neither list is authored yet; this is the arithmetic of adopting both.
1108	
1109	| Set | `S_int` as authored | + instruments | + consoles | `S_int` with both | vs 120 | `S_total` (+ 30) | vs 192 |
1110	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
1111	| S0 `{home}` | 68 | 9 | 1 | 78 | pass | 108 | pass |
1112	| S1 `{home, A}` | 100 | 14 | 2 | 116 | pass (4 slack) | 146 | pass |
1113	| S2, S3 `{home, B}` / `{home+B}` | 112 | 14 | 2 | 128 | **over by 8** | 158 | pass |
1114	| **S4 `{home+B, A}`** | 144 | 19 | 3 | **166** | **over by 46** | **196** | **over by 4** |
1115	
1116	I-7 for a budget of 166: 166 + 24 = 190 and ceil(4 x 190 / 3) = **254**, which leaves `S_total` 196 with 58 spare. The 25-subject diet (S4 144 to 119 as authored) is no longer enough, because it leaves 141 against 120 with both lists placed, and S2 and S3 would breach 120 where the diet never reached. **Intended route:** ASK-I1 (register by body adjacency or proximity, so a far welded section does not spend the budget) or a joint raise to about 166 with `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` about 254; the diet is the last resort, because it removes restorable modules from a game whose pillar is that wrecks have usable organs (P5). S4 reachability is never gated *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
1117	
1118	**User ruling D37 and the registered neighbourhood (2026-10-27).** Interaction registers interactable subjects by body adjacency or proximity and not by "loaded" (ASK-I1 adopted). Define a neighbourhood N as the player's body plus any body adjacent to it; in the MVP a pod-docked derelict is a separate body (BDY-25) and is not adjacent to the home body, and a welded B belongs to the home body `[UNV: Interaction IA-37, the adjacency predicate]`, and the proximity radius is `[PLACEHOLDER: Interaction]`. The gate becomes `SUBJECT_BUDGET_SET iff S_adj(N) = F(N) + L_seed(N) + C > INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET`, with `C` counted once. Worked example with the DA-47 slots: {home} 50 + 2 + 18 = **70**; {A} 28 + 4 + 18 = **50**; {B unwelded} 40 + 4 + 18 = **62**; {home+B} 90 + 6 + 18 = **114**, so the worst case is 114, at most 120 with 6 slack, and S4 `{home+B, A}` (146 as a sum) is never a registered state. With the instruments and consoles of OQ-DA-38 and OQ-DA-39 the neighbourhoods are {home} 70 + 9 + 1 = 80, {A} 50 + 5 + 1 = 56 and {home+B} 114 + 14 + 2 = **130, over by 10**, so the {home+B} rows wait for Interaction's proximity radius and not for a budget raise. The Emitter side is unchanged: `S_total` stays judged on the loaded set, 146 + 30 = 176 of 192 as authored (16 spare) and 168 + 30 = 198 with both lists (6 over), which is one more reason those rows are not authored yet. The I-7 and cumulative arithmetic above is the record of the pre-ruling route and used 68, 100, 112, 112 and 144 (add 2 to each for DA-47) Registry `subject_budget` (Interaction-owned) states the lint as the registration-window form `W_int(p) = F + L_seed + C <= INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` 120 at every authored body position, summed over the registration window plus its one-hop ring (`SUBJECT_WINDOW_HOPS`), with the S4 WARN retired and `P + Y <= PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE` 24 (`Y` the salvage-yield ITEM subjects); where this paragraph says "neighbourhood N" or "adjacency", read that window, and the loaded-set `S_int` formula above is the INFO upper bound only *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
